enzyme_name: none - spontaneous arene-oxide to phenol rearrangement (NIH shift)
organism_context: mammalian CYP2E1-mediated bromobenzene metabolism; the epoxide itself aromatizes without a protein
rationale: KEGG R07073 carries no ENZYME line, no ORTHOLOGY and the explicit COMMENT 'non enzymatic': the 3,4-arene oxide made by cytochrome P450 aromatizes spontaneously to 4-bromophenol. No protein catalyses this step, so no mono/bi/poly call applies.
direction_note: Arene-oxide aromatization to the phenol is a one-way chemical rearrangement; ModelSEED's '<' would have the stable phenol re-epoxidize, which cannot happen without O2 and a P450.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous arene-oxide to phenol rearrangement (NIH shift)
organism_context: mammalian bromobenzene metabolism (CYP-generated 2,3-oxide)
rationale: KEGG R07074 has no ENZYME and no ORTHOLOGY line; it is the 2,3-isomer of R07073, which KEGG explicitly comments is 'non enzymatic'. Same uncatalysed aromatization chemistry, so there is no enzyme to classify. Medium confidence only because KEGG did not repeat the comment on this entry.
direction_note: The epoxide-to-phenol direction is thermodynamically and chemically one-way; the reverse would require a P450 plus O2, which the equation does not contain.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous arene-oxide to phenol rearrangement (NIH shift)
organism_context: mammalian benzo[a]pyrene metabolism (CYP1A1/1B1-generated 9,10-oxide)
rationale: KEGG R07086 carries the COMMENT 'non enzymatic' with no EC and no orthology: benzo[a]pyrene-9,10-oxide isomerizes spontaneously to 9-hydroxybenzo[a]pyrene. There is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: Aromatization of the arene oxide is irreversible; reverting the phenol to the epoxide requires a monooxygenase and O2 that this entry does not contain.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (uncatalysed) hydration of chloral to chloral hydrate
organism_context: mammalian trichloroethylene/chloral metabolism
rationale: KEGG R07101 has no ENZYME and no ORTHOLOGY line and is annotated only as 'hydration'. Chloral is one of the classic aldehydes whose gem-diol dominates at equilibrium, and the hydration proceeds without catalysis, so no enzyme exists to classify.
direction_note: The hydrate is overwhelmingly favoured for trichloroacetaldehyde, so the ModelSEED '<' (dehydration of chloral hydrate back to chloral) is the minor direction; this is set by chemistry, not by any enzyme.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - mercapturic-acid pathway: gamma-glutamyltransferase, cysteinylglycine dipeptidase, then cysteine S-conjugate N-acetyltransferase
organism_context: mammalian kidney/liver processing of ethylene-oxide-derived glutathione conjugates
rationale: KEGG R07118 itself comments 'several steps reaction' and gives no EC: converting the S-(2-hydroxyethyl)glutathione conjugate to the N-acetylcysteine (mercapturate) takes three separate enzymes (GGT removes glutamate, a dipeptidase removes glycine, NAT8 acetylates), so no single protein catalyses the entry and ModelSEED flags it mass-imbalanced (MI:C:-5/H:-8/N:-2/O:-3).
direction_note: Every step of the mercapturate route is effectively irreversible (peptide-bond hydrolysis then acetyl-CoA-driven acetylation), so flux runs GSH-conjugate to mercapturate, the LLM direction; the reverse would require re-synthesising a tripeptide from an N-acetylcysteine.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - chemical N7-guanine alkylation by the episulfonium ion followed by mercapturic-acid processing
organism_context: 1,2-dihaloethane / ethylene dibromide genotoxicity via glutathione conjugation
rationale: KEGG R07119 is annotated 'unclear reaction' with no EC or orthology, and ModelSEED flags it mass- and charge-imbalanced (MI:H:-4/N:3/O:-2|CI:-1) because the guanine acceptor and the glutamate/glycine/acetyl changes are all missing. It lumps a non-enzymatic DNA-alkylation with multi-enzyme mercapturate formation, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: The glutathione episulfonium ion is a reactive electrophile that alkylates guanine N7 irreversibly; the ModelSEED '<' direction (regenerating the episulfonium ion from a DNA adduct) is not a real process.

enzyme_name: sarcosine/dimethylglycine N-methyltransferase (SDMT); the same step is also run by glycine sarcosine N-methyltransferase (GSMT)
organism_context: Halorhodospira (Ectothiorhodospira) halochloris, Aphanothece halophytica, Methanohalophilus portucalensis - halophile glycine-betaine osmolyte biosynthesis
rationale: Nyyssola et al. expressed and purified GSMT and SDMT of E. halochloris as two separate, highly substrate-specific SAM-dependent methyltransferases; each carries one catalytic activity (N-methyl transfer) applied to successive amine substrates, so the several EC numbers (2.1.1.156/157/162) record substrate range rather than fused domains. The Methanohalophilus 'GSDMT' with all three activities is a 240 kDa four-subunit assembly, which the multi-subunit-complex exclusion also keeps monofunctional.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way (betaine accumulation under osmotic stress); the enzyme does not run SAH-dependent demethylation of dimethylglycine, so ModelSEED's '<' is unsupported.

enzyme_name: lovastatin nonaketide synthase (LovB / LNKS), assisted in trans by the enoyl reductase LovC and the thioesterase LovG
distinct_activities: Diels-Alderase/cyclization activity attributed to the KS region
organism_context: Aspergillus terreus; LovB is a single ~335 kDa polypeptide, its own ER domain is non-functional
rationale: LovB is a single-chain iterative highly-reducing type I PKS carrying KS, MAT, DH, C-MeT, KR and ACP catalytic domains on one polypeptide (reconstituted in vitro by Ma et al.); because its ER domain is inactive, LovC supplies the enoyl reductions and LovG releases dihydromonacolin L, so IUBMB describes EC 2.3.1.161 as a two-protein enzyme system.
direction_note: ModelSEED omits the whole product side (CoA, CO2, NADP+, SAH, H2O; status MI:C:-442), so the ' < ' call reflects a nonsense equation; nine decarboxylative Claisen condensations plus NADPH consumption make polyketide assembly irreversibly biosynthetic.

organism_context: Penicillium patulum/griseofulvum, Aspergillus terreus, Pseudallescheria boydii; homotetramer of a ~190 kDa chain
rationale: 6-MSAS is a single ~190 kDa iterative type I PKS polypeptide with KS, AT, DH, KR and ACP domains that carries out three condensations, one ketoreduction, dehydration, cyclization and thioester hydrolysis; IUBMB/KEGG describe EC 2.3.1.165 as a self-contained multienzyme needing no partner protein (one orthology, K15320).
direction_note: ModelSEED drops NADP+ and H2O from the products (status MI:C:-21), but the three decarboxylations and the thioester hydrolysis make 6-methylsalicylate formation irreversible in the forward direction regardless.

enzyme_name: chalcone synthase (CHS) acting together with chalcone/polyketide reductase (CHR)
organism_context: legumes (Glycyrrhiza, Medicago, Glycine max) - 5-deoxy(iso)flavonoid branch
rationale: EC 2.3.1.170 is not one protein: a monofunctional type III PKS (CHS, a homodimer with a single condensing/cyclizing active site) builds the tetraketide, and a physically separate monofunctional aldo-keto reductase (CHR) reduces the CHS-bound intermediate before cyclization to isoliquiritigenin - they have to be co-expressed or co-localized to give the 6'-deoxychalcone. Under the complex exclusion, CHS, the subunit running the acyltransfer, is monofunctional.
direction_note: Three decarboxylative condensations plus CoA release make this irreversibly biosynthetic; ModelSEED also drops NADP+/H2O (status MI:C:-21), so its ' < ' is an artefact rather than enzymology.

organism_context: Hordeum vulgare (barley), Oryza sativa, Zea mays - Strategy II graminaceous iron acquisition
rationale: Barley naat-A and naat-B encode single-domain class-I PLP-dependent aminotransferases that transfer the amino group of nicotianamine to 2-oxoglutarate; no second catalytic activity is reported for the NAAT family in the cloning paper or in the later maize genome-wide survey.
direction_note: Transamination is intrinsically near-equilibrium, but in planta NAAT is committed forward because the 3''-oxo product is immediately reduced by deoxymugineic-acid synthase; the ModelSEED '<' would run the phytosiderophore pathway backwards.

enzyme_name: bile acid / hydroxysteroid sulfotransferase (SULT2A1; rat BAST I; mouse Sult2a8)
organism_context: human and rodent liver cytosol
rationale: SULT2A1 is a single-domain cytosolic sulfotransferase (homodimer) whose sole catalytic activity is PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer onto 3-hydroxy steroids and bile acids including glycolithocholate; the mouse dedicated bile-acid sulfonator Sult2a8 has the same single-domain SULT fold.
direction_note: PAPS-driven sulfonation releasing PAP is physiologically irreversible and sulfoglycolithocholate is an excreted detoxification end product; desulfation is the job of a separate sulfatase, not of this enzyme, so '<' misassigns the chemistry.

organism_context: Thermotoga maritima (TM1643/NadX), Archaeoglobus fulgidus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Ralstonia eutropha
rationale: A small Rossmann-fold NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenase first identified from the structure/function study of T. maritima TM1643; it carries only the oxidative-deamination activity and supplies iminoaspartate to quinolinate synthase for de novo NAD biosynthesis.
direction_note: The isolated enzyme is reversible in vitro (it is even exploited for reductive amination to L-aspartate), but its physiological role is oxidative deamination pulled forward by NadA consuming the unstable iminoaspartate, so the forward (LLM) call matches the biology.

organism_context: Thermotoga maritima NadX (NAD+-preferring), Archaeoglobus fulgidus, Klebsiella pneumoniae
rationale: Same single-activity Rossmann-fold dehydrogenase as the NADP+ entry; the characterized T. maritima and archaeal enzymes are one-domain proteins with no second catalytic function, differing only in nicotinamide-cofactor preference.
direction_note: In vivo the enzyme runs oxidative deamination because quinolinate synthase removes the unstable iminoaspartate product; the thermodynamic '<' preference is overridden by that downstream pull.

enzyme_name: hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase (HQT; the paralogous HCT prefers shikimate)
organism_context: Solanaceae (tomato, tobacco), Coffea, Cynara, Carthamus - chlorogenic acid biosynthesis; HCT orthologues in lignifying tissue of poplar/Brachypodium/bryophytes
rationale: HQT/HCT are single-domain BAHD-family acyltransferases with one catalytic histidine and a single transacylation activity; their dual quinate/shikimate acceptor use is substrate promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: BAHD transacylation is genuinely reversible - HCT is well documented to run ester-to-CoA-thioester during lignin biosynthesis - so direction is set by the acyl-CoA/quinate pools; in chlorogenic-acid-accumulating tissue the net flux is ester formation, i.e. the LLM's forward sense, but neither fixed call is right in general.

organism_context: E. coli, Bacillus subtilis, Sulfolobus tokodaii, Thermococcus litoralis, Arabidopsis thaliana (AO/FIN4)
rationale: NadB is a single-chain FAD flavoprotein of the succinate dehydrogenase/fumarate reductase fold with one active site that dehydrogenates L-aspartate to iminoaspartate; its ability to reoxidize the flavin with either O2 (aerobic) or fumarate (anaerobic) is a choice of electron acceptor at the same site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: The real oxidant is missing: ModelSEED writes free FAD/FADH2 as substrate/product in place of the tightly bound prosthetic group and omits O2 (or fumarate), removing exactly the term that makes aspartate oxidation irreversible and producing the spurious '<' preference.

organism_context: mammalian/fungal glycogen synthesis; the bacterial GlgA orthologue uses ADP-glucose
rationale: Glycogen synthase is a single-domain GT-B glycosyltransferase (structurally homologous to glycogen phosphorylase) with one transglucosylation activity; glycogenin and branching enzyme are separate proteins it associates with. Confidence is medium only because ModelSEED merges five EC numbers into this one entry (2.4.1.11 glycogen, 2.4.1.12 cellulose, 2.4.1.34 1,3-beta-glucan, 2.4.1.168 xyloglucan, 2.4.1.183 synthases), so more than one distinct enzyme is actually covered.
direction_note: ModelSEED strips the glucan acceptor and product (status MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5), so the entry reads 'UDP-glucose -> UDP' and the thermodynamic estimate is for a non-reaction; glucosyl transfer from UDP-glucose onto a growing glucan is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way.

organism_context: E. coli DNA polymerase I (polA) is the single-chain three-activity enzyme; the replicative Pol III holoenzyme is instead a multi-subunit complex whose alpha subunit (dnaE) carries the polymerase alone
rationale: Bacterial Pol I, the textbook family-A polymerase, carries polymerase, 3'->5' proofreading and 5'->3' nick-translation exonuclease activities on one polypeptide, so dNTP incorporation as written is run by a genuinely polyfunctional chain in that case; medium confidence because the bulk replicative flux in vivo goes through Pol III, a multi-subunit complex that would be scored monofunctional for its alpha subunit.
direction_note: The DNA primer and extended product are deleted (status MI:C:-10/H:-12/N:-5/O:-5/P:-1), leaving 'dATP -> PPi'; real polymerization is pulled forward by inorganic pyrophosphatase hydrolysing the released PPi, so the thermodynamics-derived '<' is meaningless here.

organism_context: E. coli DNA polymerase I (polA); Pol III holoenzyme is a multi-subunit complex instead
rationale: Same enzyme as the dATP entry, differing only in the incoming nucleotide: Pol I is one polypeptide with polymerase plus two distinct exonuclease activities, whereas the replicative Pol III is a complex of separate subunits, which the complex exclusion would keep monofunctional.
direction_note: With the DNA substrate/product removed the entry reduces to 'dGTP -> PPi'; in vivo polymerization is made irreversible by pyrophosphatase, so the '<' call rests on a degenerate equation.

organism_context: E. coli DNA polymerase I (polA); Pol III holoenzyme is a multi-subunit complex instead
rationale: Same polymerase as the other three dNTP entries; Pol I fuses polymerase, proofreading exonuclease and 5'->3' exonuclease on one chain, while Pol III achieves the equivalent by assembling separate subunits (alpha polymerase, epsilon proofreader), which is a complex, not a fused enzyme.
direction_note: 'dCTP -> PPi' with the DNA stripped out is not a real reaction; pyrophosphatase-coupled polymerization runs one way, so the LLM's forward call is the right one.

organism_context: E. coli DNA polymerase I (polA); Pol III holoenzyme is a multi-subunit complex instead
rationale: The dTTP incorporation step of the same EC 2.7.7.7 activity; family-A Pol I is the polyfunctional single-chain case, Pol III the multi-subunit alternative whose alpha subunit alone would score monofunctional.
direction_note: DNA is absent from both sides (status MI:C:-10/H:-13/N:-2/O:-7/P:-1); genuine polymerization is driven forward by PPi hydrolysis.

organism_context: E. coli pcnB-encoded PAP I; eukaryotic canonical nuclear poly(A) polymerase
rationale: PAP I is a single-chain pol-beta-superfamily nucleotidyltransferase whose only catalytic activity is template-independent AMP addition to RNA 3' ends (its regulation by tyrosine phosphorylation and its horizontal-transfer distribution are both described for a one-activity protein). The additional EC numbers ModelSEED attaches here (2.7.7.6/2.7.7.48) belong to multi-subunit RNA polymerases, which the complex exclusion also keeps out of the bifunctional category.
direction_note: The RNA acceptor and extended product are deleted (status MI:C:-10/H:-12/N:-5/O:-6/P:-1), so 'ATP -> PPi' is all that is left; adenylyl transfer is pulled forward in vivo by pyrophosphatase.

organism_context: bacterial alpha2-beta-beta'-omega core RNAP; eukaryotic Pol I/II/III are likewise multi-subunit
rationale: This is one GTP-incorporation step of transcription, catalysed by the multi-subunit RNA polymerase assembly, which has a single nucleotidyl-transfer active site formed at the beta/beta' interface. A complex of separate polypeptides is explicitly not a fused bifunctional enzyme, so the catalysing entity scores monofunctional; called from established knowledge rather than a dedicated search.
direction_note: With the RNA chain removed the entry degenerates to 'GTP -> PPi' (status MI:C:-10/...); transcription is driven forward by PPi hydrolysis, so the LLM's forward sense is correct.

organism_context: bacterial alpha2-beta-beta'-omega core RNAP; eukaryotic Pol I/II/III are likewise multi-subunit
rationale: The CTP-incorporation step of the same multi-subunit RNA polymerase; separate subunits assembling into one active site is a complex, not a fused bifunctional chain, so monofunctional is the honest call. Based on established knowledge, no literature search needed.
direction_note: 'CTP -> PPi' with the RNA product stripped out is not a real reaction; chain elongation runs forward because pyrophosphatase removes the PPi.

enzyme_name: DNA-directed RNA polymerase (core enzyme); the EC 2.7.7.52 variant is a terminal uridylyltransferase (Cid1/TUT4/URT1)
organism_context: bacterial multi-subunit RNAP; S. pombe Cid1 and human TUT4/ZCCHC11 for the template-independent uridylylation activity
rationale: Both candidate enzymes for this entry carry a single nucleotidyl-transfer activity: the RNAP core is a multi-subunit complex with one catalytic site (excluded from bifunctional by the complex rule), and Cid1/TUT4-type poly(U) polymerases are single-chain pol-beta-superfamily nucleotidyltransferases with no second catalytic function.
direction_note: The RNA acceptor and extended product are missing (status MI:C:-9/H:-11/N:-2/O:-8/P:-1), leaving 'UTP -> PPi'; uridylyl transfer is made irreversible in vivo by pyrophosphate hydrolysis.
